pa0.premise: Xenia's weekly timetable at the conservatory: theory on Mondays at nine, piano on Tuesdays and Thursdays at two, choir on Wednesdays at six in the evening, and orchestra on Fridays at ten. Piano lessons last an hour; all other classes last ninety minutes. She has no other scheduled classes. This week every class took place as timetabled and she attended all of them.
pa0.hypothesis: Xenia spent six and a half hours in scheduled classes this week.

pa1.premise: Klara's bakery sells out of rye bread most Saturdays by noon. Klara bakes 40 rye loaves on Saturdays and 25 on other days. Last Saturday a coach party arrived at eleven and bought bread, pastries and coffee. Klara later told her sister it had been the busiest morning of the year, and that she had barely sat down. Klara has run the bakery for nine years.
pa1.hypothesis: Klara's bakery sold out of rye bread before noon last Saturday.

pa2.premise: At the Oberlin family dinner, Greta sat between her brother Wim and her cousin Lise. Wim's wife, Nadia, sat directly opposite Wim. Lise's father is the brother of Greta's mother. Nadia's parents were not present, but Wim's parents were, and they sat at the head and foot of the table. Nobody changed seats during the meal, and the table seated eight.
pa2.hypothesis: Greta's uncle's child sat next to Greta.

pa3.premise: Nils's flight lands at 14:10. The airport train to the city runs every twenty minutes, and the journey takes 35 minutes. Nils allows 45 minutes from landing to reach the train platform. He has a meeting in the city at 15:30, and it takes ten minutes to walk from the city station to the meeting room. He has no other way of getting into the city.
pa3.hypothesis: If Nils's flight lands on time and everything goes as he has allowed, he can reach the meeting before 15:30.

pa4.premise: Ignatius keeps a log of rainfall at his farm. The totals for the last four weeks were 12, 8, 21 and 15 millimetres. His neighbour, Gwyneth, uses the same type of gauge and recorded 14, 9, 19 and 17 millimetres for the same four weeks. Both gauges were checked afterwards and found to be accurate, and neither log has any missing days.
pa4.hypothesis: Ignatius recorded more rain than Gwyneth over the four weeks.

pa5.premise: Anselm's allotment neighbour, Rhoda, keeps bees at the far end of her plot. Last year she gave Anselm three jars of honey in return for his help repairing her shed. This year the shed did not need repairing, and Anselm spent most of his time on his own beans. In September Rhoda mentioned over the fence that the hives had produced less than last year.
pa5.hypothesis: Rhoda gave Anselm honey this year.

pa6.premise: Halvor's bakery order for the wedding: 120 bread rolls, 3 large loaves and 40 sweet buns, to be collected at ten on Saturday morning. Halvor confirmed by phone on Thursday that everything would be ready. On Saturday, Perrine collected the order at half past ten and drove straight to the venue without stopping. The rolls were still warm when she arrived.
pa6.hypothesis: Perrine arrived at the venue before eleven.

pa7.premise: Renske has two children, Bram and Fenna. Bram is fourteen. Fenna turned eleven in February of this year. Renske's sister Lotte has one child, Jip, who was born in the same calendar year as Fenna but whose birthday is in November. The two families see each other most weekends. It is now July, and the cousins are spending the school holiday together at Lotte's house by the lake.

pa8.premise: Elsbeth keeps three hens. The brown one lays every day, the white one lays every second day, and the speckled one has not laid since spring. Elsbeth collects the eggs each evening and sells them in boxes of six to her neighbour. Over the last fourteen days she collected every egg laid and none were broken; the white hen laid on seven of those days and the speckled hen laid none.
pa8.hypothesis: Elsbeth collected 21 eggs in the last fourteen days.

pa9.premise: The Ridgeway youth football league requires that every player on a team's match sheet be under fourteen years of age on the first day of the season, which was 1 September this year. Team sheets are checked after the match. Callum was born on 30 August, exactly fourteen years before this season began. He played the full match for Marston Juniors on 12 September.
pa9.hypothesis: Callum was eligible for the Marston Juniors match under the league's age rule.

pa10.premise: At the Kettleby community meeting, residents raised concerns about the new streetlights on Mill Row, which some said were too bright. The council representative, Mr. Hobbes, said the lights met national guidance and that dimming them would require an engineering assessment. He agreed to request the assessment. A resident named Tanith asked whether the assessment would be made public. Mr. Hobbes said he would find out.
pa10.hypothesis: The streetlights on Mill Row will be dimmed.

pa11.premise: Beatrice's mother told her that the family's clock had been bought by her great-grandfather from a clockmaker in Ashcombe. Beatrice found the clockmaker's name, Pargeter, engraved inside the case. A trade directory from the period lists a Pargeter as a clockmaker in Ashcombe. Beatrice has not found any receipt or other record of the purchase in the family papers. The clock still keeps good time.
pa11.hypothesis: Beatrice's great-grandfather bought the clock from Pargeter.

pa12.premise: Corinne and her flatmate Yusuf share the cost of groceries equally, settling up at the end of each month. In March Corinne paid 310 units and Yusuf paid 190. In April Yusuf paid for everything, a total of 480 units. Corinne kept April's receipts in a drawer and has not yet added them up, and neither of them has mentioned March since it ended.
pa12.hypothesis: At the end of April, Corinne owed Yusuf 180 units.

pa13.premise: The Tremayne bookshop keeps a list of customers who want to be told when a particular title comes back into stock. Ivo asked to be added to the list for a poetry collection in June. The collection came back into stock in August, and the shop sent messages to everyone on the list. Ivo bought the collection in September, from the Tremayne bookshop, and paid in cash.
pa13.hypothesis: Ivo received the shop's message about the poetry collection.

pa14.premise: The Beaumont Street clinic's records show that Mr. Feld's blood pressure was measured at 150 over 95 in January and 138 over 88 in April. The clinic's guideline treats a reading as high when either number is at or above 140 over 90 respectively. Mr. Feld was prescribed a new medication in February and has taken it daily since. He has not changed his diet.
pa14.hypothesis: Mr. Feld's April reading was classified as high under the clinic's guideline.

pa15.premise: Yolanda and Bram share the driving on their delivery round. Whoever drives in the morning does not drive in the afternoon, and one of the two always drives each session. On Monday Bram drove in the morning. On Tuesday Yolanda drove in the morning. On Wednesday the morning driver was the same person as Monday's afternoon driver. The round runs every weekday, morning and afternoon.

pa16.premise: Mirabel is training for a half marathon in October. Her plan has her running four times a week, with a long run on Sundays. In August she missed two long runs because of a family wedding and a cold. Her coach, Dagny, said the plan had enough margin for a couple of missed sessions. Mirabel completed every session in September and felt strong.
pa16.hypothesis: Mirabel completed the half marathon in October.

pa17.premise: Sunniva's grandmother's recipe for gingerbread calls for dark syrup, but Sunniva only had light syrup and used that instead. She also reduced the sugar by a quarter because she was baking for her father, who has been told to cut down on sugar. The gingerbread came out paler than usual. Her father ate three pieces with his coffee and asked for the recipe.
pa17.hypothesis: Sunniva's father noticed that the gingerbread was less sweet than usual.

pa18.premise: Rafaela's contract with the Merriman agency pays a flat fee of 1,200 units per article, with a bonus of 300 units for any article that is picked up by a national outlet. Last quarter she wrote five articles for the agency. Her total payment for the quarter was 6,600 units. She has not yet received a statement showing which articles earned the bonus.
pa18.hypothesis: Rafaela's two most recent articles earned the bonus.

pa19.premise: The Marlowe Street bakery opens at six every morning except Sunday, when it opens at eight. Its sourdough loaves sell out most days before ten. Cato lives two doors down and buys a sourdough loaf every Saturday on his way to the market. Last Saturday he left home at a quarter past nine and returned twenty minutes later carrying a paper bag from the bakery and a bunch of flowers.
pa19.hypothesis: Cato bought a sourdough loaf last Saturday.

pa20.premise: The Okonkwo children take turns doing the dishes: Ada on Mondays and Thursdays, Emeka on Tuesdays and Fridays, and Ngozi on Wednesdays and Saturdays. On Sundays their father does them. If a child is away, the next child in the rotation covers that day, and the rotation order is Ada, then Emeka, then Ngozi, then back to Ada. Emeka was away all of last week from Monday to Sunday, and nobody else was away.
pa20.hypothesis: Last week, Ngozi did the dishes on four days.

pa21.premise: The Pemberton Prize jury shortlists five novels each year, always including at least one debut. This year's shortlist contained two debuts. One of the debuts, by an author named Kalinda, was later withdrawn because it had been published a year earlier than the rules allow, and it was replaced by a non-debut novel. The jury did not change any other entries before the winner was announced.
pa21.hypothesis: The final shortlist contained exactly one debut novel.

pa22.premise: The Rowan Street residents' association charges an annual fee of 24 units, payable in January, or 2 units per month for those who prefer to pay monthly, with the first monthly payment due in January. Anyone joining mid-year pays only for the remaining months of that year at the monthly rate, including the month of joining. Isidora joined in September and paid exactly what she owed for the year.

pa23.premise: The Aldous Library fines borrowers 1 unit per day for overdue books, capped at 20 units per book. Fines are waived for borrowers under sixteen. Jorunn returned a book that was 25 days overdue and was not charged anything. The librarian, Petrus, stamped the return card, put the book on the trolley, and said nothing about a fine. Jorunn thanked him and left with two new books.

pa24.premise: Hollis Books orders stock from two suppliers. Supplier A delivers within three working days of an order and charges no delivery fee for orders over 200 units. Supplier B delivers on the next working day but charges 15 units per delivery regardless of size. On Monday the shop ordered 350 units of stock from Supplier B and 120 units from Supplier A. Both suppliers confirmed the orders.
pa24.hypothesis: The shop received both orders by Wednesday.

pa25.premise: Ambrose runs the Saturday morning parkrun timing. Runners are given a finish token in order of crossing the line, numbered from 1 upward. This week 142 runners finished. Tokens 1 to 50 are blue, 51 to 100 are yellow, and all higher numbers are red. Ambrose's own daughter Clemency finished with token 97 and handed it in at the scanning table.

pa26.premise: The Auberon choir rehearses on Tuesday evenings. Members who miss three consecutive rehearsals, each without giving notice in advance, are removed from the concert list, though they remain members. Ferdinand missed the rehearsals on the 5th, 12th and 19th. He sent an apology to the director before the rehearsal on the 12th, but gave no notice for the other two. No other member missed more than one rehearsal that month.
pa26.hypothesis: Ferdinand was removed from the concert list under the rule.

pa27.premise: The Vilhelm Prize committee accepts nominations only from past winners, and each past winner may nominate one candidate per year. There are seven living past winners. This year five of them submitted nominations, and two of those nominated the same candidate, a botanist named Carys. No candidate may be nominated for work already recognised by the prize, and all nominations this year were valid.
pa27.hypothesis: This year the committee received nominations for five distinct candidates.

pa28.premise: The Hallam Street school asks parents to sign a consent form before pupils go on any trip. The year six trip to the Ridley marshes is on Friday. Forms were due back on Wednesday. On Thursday afternoon the class teacher, Mr. Voss, had forms from every pupil except Tarquin. Tarquin's mother works nights and is hard to reach by phone.
pa28.hypothesis: Tarquin did not go on the trip to the Ridley marshes.

pa29.premise: The Silverlake Hotel charges 120 units per night for a standard room and 180 units per night for a suite. Breakfast is included for suite guests and costs 15 units per person per day for standard-room guests. Ludovic booked two nights and was charged a total of 270 units for his stay. His booking confirmation lists one guest and the hotel's stated rates were applied without any discount.
pa29.hypothesis: Ludovic stayed in a suite for both nights.

pa30.premise: Britt's employer reimburses travel to client sites at 0.4 units per kilometre if staff use their own car, and pays the full fare if they use public transport. Britt visited the Northam site three times last month. The site is 60 kilometres from the office by road. Her approved expense claim for the month came to 144 units for travel, with nothing else claimed.
pa30.hypothesis: Britt drove her own car to the Northam site on all three visits.

pa31.premise: The Nethercott village hall can be booked in the morning, afternoon or evening. A booking for two consecutive sessions on the same day is charged at 150 percent of the single-session rate, and three consecutive sessions at twice the rate. The single-session rate is 40 units. The Harlow family booked the afternoon and evening sessions on one Saturday for a christening party and paid the standard charge.
pa31.hypothesis: The Harlow family was charged 80 units for the hall.

pa32.premise: Rules for the Hartwell allotments: bonfires are permitted only on Saturdays between October and March, and never within ten metres of any shed. Water butts must be covered. Plot 14 has a shed at its northern edge and measures eight metres from north to south. Its holder, Ines, lit a bonfire at the southern edge of plot 14 on a Saturday in November, and it burned for an hour.
pa32.hypothesis: Ines's bonfire complied with the Hartwell allotment rules.

pa33.premise: Ferran's itinerary: depart Vossmark by train at 08:10, arriving at Quillhaven at 11:35. A bus leaves Quillhaven station for the coast every 40 minutes starting at 09:00. The coastal ride takes 55 minutes. Ferran needs to be at the harbour by 14:00 for a boat that will not wait. He plans to buy lunch at Quillhaven station before boarding the bus, which he estimates takes 20 minutes.
pa33.hypothesis: If the train is on time and lunch takes the estimated 20 minutes, the first bus Ferran can catch after lunch reaches the coast at 13:15.

pa34.premise: The Marlbury station car park has 200 spaces. On weekdays, 150 spaces are reserved for season-ticket holders until nine in the morning, after which any driver may use them. The remaining 50 spaces are always open to all. On Tuesday at eight in the morning, 140 season-ticket holders and 50 other drivers were parked, and no one else. Every driver parked legitimately.
pa34.hypothesis: At eight on Tuesday, there were ten spaces available to a season-ticket holder and none available to other drivers.

pa35.premise: The Corrigan family has a rule that screens are off by eight on school nights. Their eldest, Maeve, is allowed to stay up until ten on Fridays and Saturdays. Last Thursday, Maeve was found watching a film at half past eight. Her father took the tablet away. The next day was a school inset day, so there were no classes for pupils, although the teachers were in.
pa35.hypothesis: Maeve broke the family's screen rule on Thursday.

pa36.premise: The Norridge weekly market runs every Saturday except the last Saturday of each month, when the square is used for the flea market instead. In October of this year, Saturdays fell on the 3rd, 10th, 17th, 24th and 31st. Stallholders pay for the weekly market by the month, at 15 units per Saturday on which the weekly market runs. Ilka rented a stall for all of October and paid exactly what was due.
pa36.hypothesis: Ilka paid 60 units for her October stall.

pa37.premise: Corvin's chess club meets on Thursdays in the back room of the Larkspur cafe. The cafe charges the club 40 units for the room, which the club covers by charging members 2 units per session. At last Thursday's session there were twenty-three members present, so the club made a small surplus. Corvin keeps any surplus in a tin behind the bar, which he says is for the annual prize.
pa37.hypothesis: The annual prize is paid entirely from session surpluses.

pa38.premise: The Whitlow apartment building has a laundry room that residents book in two-hour slots. Each apartment may hold at most two bookings per week, and bookings cannot be transferred between apartments. Apartment 5B booked Monday morning and Thursday evening this week. Apartment 5C booked nothing. On Wednesday, the tenant of 5B asked 5C's tenant to book a Saturday slot for her to use.
pa38.hypothesis: If 5C's tenant makes the Saturday booking, 5B's tenant may use it under the building's rules.

pa39.premise: Lorcan's bicycle shop offers a free tune-up within thirty days of purchase. After that, tune-ups cost 25 units, or 15 units for members of the Cowley Cycling Club. Fenwick bought a bicycle from Lorcan on 3 May and brought it back for a tune-up on 10 June, when the shop was quiet. He was charged 15 units, paid by card, and rode home the same afternoon.
pa39.hypothesis: Fenwick's tune-up on 10 June was free under the thirty-day offer.

pa40.premise: Notice from the Brackenfield council: household waste collections will move from Tuesdays to Wednesdays starting the week of the 15th. Recycling collections are unaffected and remain on alternate Fridays. The first Wednesday collection will be on the 17th. Residents should not put bins out on Tuesday the 16th, as no collection will take place that day. Garden waste subscriptions are suspended until spring.
pa40.hypothesis: Before the change, Brackenfield household waste was collected on Wednesdays.

pa41.premise: Tavia's morning routine: she wakes at 6:10, runs for 35 minutes starting at 6:20, showers for 15 minutes immediately after the run, and leaves for work exactly 20 minutes after finishing her shower. Her commute takes 25 minutes door to door. Yesterday she followed the routine exactly in every respect, except that her run took 10 minutes longer than usual.
pa41.hypothesis: Tavia arrived at work at 8:05 yesterday.

pa42.premise: The Vallery Hotel does not allow guests to bring their own food into the dining room, and it does not serve dinner after nine. Room service is available until eleven, but only for guests staying in the tower wing. Aurelio checked in on Thursday evening and was given a room on the fourth floor. At half past nine he asked at reception whether he could still get dinner, and the receptionist checked his room number.
pa42.hypothesis: Aurelio was able to order dinner from room service.

pa43.premise: Tobias's employer pays overtime at one and a half times the hourly rate for hours beyond forty in a week. Tobias's hourly rate is 20 units. Last week he was on site for 46 hours, including a one-hour unpaid lunch each day over five days. His timesheet for the week has not yet been approved by his supervisor, who is away until Wednesday.
pa43.hypothesis: Tobias will be paid overtime for last week.

pa44.premise: Marisol runs the front desk at the Halvane Clinic on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. On the other two weekdays the desk is covered by Teodor, except when Teodor is on leave, in which case Marisol covers his shifts as well. Teodor took leave for the whole week of the fourteenth. The clinic is closed on weekends, and nobody works the desk on public holidays. There were no public holidays in the week of the fourteenth, and the clinic was open every weekday as usual.
pa44.hypothesis: During the week of the fourteenth, Marisol worked the front desk on five days.

pa45.premise: The Ashdown Players are staging a comedy in three acts. Ticket sales for the opening night were strong, and the director, Mortimer, added a Sunday matinee. The lead actress, Cordelia, has a cold. Her understudy, Pip, rehearsed the role on Wednesday. The company's newsletter promised that all advertised performances would go ahead whatever happened. The play runs for four nights at the village theatre.
pa45.hypothesis: Pip performed the lead role on opening night.

pa46.premise: Sample tubes are centrifuged for six minutes at the low setting, then the supernatant is drawn off with a fresh pipette tip. She logged that all twelve were centrifuged and resuspended before 10:30, and that she began the next step on the batch at 10:45.

pa47.premise: Olafur teaches the beginners' pottery class on Monday evenings and the intermediate class on Wednesday evenings. Students may move from beginners to intermediate once they have completed eight sessions and Olafur has approved the move. Dalia joined the beginners' class in September and has attended every session since. There have been ten beginners' sessions so far this term. The studio is on the ground floor of the old mill.
pa47.hypothesis: Dalia has moved to the intermediate class.

pa48.premise: The Harrowgate bus company operates route 12 between the station and the hospital every fifteen minutes from six in the morning until midnight. On Sundays the frequency drops to every thirty minutes and the last bus leaves at ten in the evening. Route 12 does not stop at the university on any day; that stop is served by route 14 only, which runs hourly.
pa48.hypothesis: On Sundays, route 12 buses run until midnight.

pa49.premise: Every dog registered with the Pellham kennel club has exactly one registered owner. Simone has registered two dogs, Biscuit and Rook. Rook's litter-mate, Bramble, is registered to Simone's neighbour, Alaric. Alaric has no other dogs registered. Biscuit is the only dog in the entire club registered as a working dog. The club's register was updated last week. Simone walks both her dogs in the park each morning.
pa49.hypothesis: Bramble is not registered as a working dog.

pa50.premise: Under the lease for the unit at 7 Corrin Lane, the tenant may keep a pet only if the landlord has given written consent in advance. Consent, once given, cannot be withdrawn during the lease term unless the pet causes damage exceeding 200 units in a single incident. Odalys, the tenant, received written consent for a cat in March. In June the cat scratched a door, and the repair invoice came to 185 units. There have been no other incidents involving the cat.
pa50.hypothesis: The landlord is entitled under the lease to withdraw consent for Odalys's cat because of the June damage.

pa51.premise: "The Farrow contract has to be signed by Friday," said Beatriz. "Legal still hasn't returned the redline," said Konrad. "Then call them," she said. "I did, twice. Ines says she'll have it by Thursday morning." "Thursday morning leaves us one day," said Beatriz. "That's enough if there are no big changes," Konrad said. Beatriz did not reply. She picked up the phone on her desk and dialled a number.

pa52.premise: The Fairmile cycling club runs three rides on Sundays: a 30-kilometre ride leaving at eight, a 60-kilometre ride leaving at half past eight, and a 100-kilometre ride leaving at nine. Riders must sign in at the clubhouse at least fifteen minutes before their ride leaves. The clubhouse opens at half past seven. Beren signed in at 8:40 and joined the only ride he was still eligible for.

pa53.premise: The soup recipe calls for two onions, three carrots, a leek and a litre of stock. The vegetables are sweated in butter for ten minutes before the stock is added, and the soup simmers for a further twenty-five minutes. It is blended and seasoned before serving. Ilario made the soup on Sunday for six guests, doubling every quantity in the recipe and serving it with bread.

pa54.premise: At the Lisle Street clinic, patients are seen in order of arrival unless a doctor or nurse marks them as urgent, in which case they are seen next. Yesterday morning Otto arrived at 8:05, Hanne at 8:10, and Pieter at 8:15. At 8:20, before anyone had been seen, the nurse marked Pieter as urgent. No other patients arrived before nine, and nobody else was marked urgent.
pa54.hypothesis: Hanne was the last of the three to be seen.

pa55.premise: Konstantin's lease on his studio ends on 31 December. His landlord has offered a renewal at a rent 12 percent higher. Konstantin told the landlord he would decide by the end of November. Meanwhile he has viewed two other studios, one cheaper and one larger. He has told his friends that the current studio's light is hard to beat, but that the rent increase is steep.
pa55.hypothesis: Konstantin will renew the lease on his current studio.

pa56.premise: The Corvello wine bar's opening hours: Tuesday to Thursday five until eleven, Friday and Saturday five until one in the morning, closed Sunday and Monday. Last orders are thirty minutes before closing. On public holidays the bar keeps Saturday hours regardless of the day of the week. Last Monday was a public holiday, and the bar followed its stated policy.
pa56.hypothesis: The bar was closed last Monday.

pa57.premise: The Danforth school's chess team has six members. Each match uses four boards, so two members sit out each match. The coach, Mrs. Ellery, rotates so that no member sits out two matches in a row. The team has played three matches this term. Ravi sat out the first match. Sunniva sat out the second. Nobody sat out more than one match this term.
pa57.hypothesis: All six members played in at least one match this term.

pa58.premise: Under the rules of the Lorimer debating society, a motion passes only if it receives more votes in favour than against, and abstentions are not counted either way. At Thursday's meeting, the motion on changing the meeting day received 14 votes in favour, 14 against, and 5 abstentions from the members. The chair, Winifred, does not vote except to break a tie, and on this occasion she voted against.
pa58.hypothesis: The motion on changing the meeting day passed.

pa59.premise: Reagent K must be kept between 2 and 8 degrees at all times, and any vial that has been outside that range must be discarded. A vial must also be discarded 14 days after it is first opened. The lab fridge log shows a temperature excursion to 12 degrees for three hours on the 9th. Vial 17 of reagent K was first opened on the 1st and has been in that fridge continuously since. Today is the 12th, and Marguerite is preparing to use vial 17.
pa59.hypothesis: Vial 17 is within its allowed storage conditions and may be used today.

pa60.premise: Signe's contract with the Ostrell agency began on 1 April and runs for exactly eighteen months. Either party may terminate early with sixty days' written notice, but notice cannot be served during the first ninety days of the contract. Signe served written notice on 28 June of the same year, and the agency acknowledged receipt the same day. Nothing else about the contract terms was varied by either party.
pa60.hypothesis: Signe's notice was served after the first ninety days of the contract had ended.

pa61.premise: Meera's phone contract gives her 200 minutes of calls per month, after which calls cost 0.1 units per minute. Calls to numbers on the same network are free and do not count towards the allowance. In May she made 180 minutes of calls to other networks and 90 minutes of calls to the same network. She made no other calls and sent no messages that month.
pa61.hypothesis: Meera exceeded her 200-minute allowance in May.

pa62.premise: Yevgenia's phone plan includes 5 gigabytes of data per month, and each additional gigabyte costs 4 units, charged in whole gigabytes rounded up. Her plan renews on the first of the month. In August she used 7.2 gigabytes. In September she used 4.9 gigabytes. Unused data does not carry over from one month to the next, and there are no other data charges.
pa62.hypothesis: Yevgenia was charged 12 units for extra data in August and nothing for extra data in September.

pa63.premise: Matthias ordered a bookcase online on the 2nd, with delivery promised within ten working days. On the 9th he received a message saying the order had been dispatched. On the 15th he had still not received it and called the retailer, who said the courier had attempted delivery on the 12th and left a card. Matthias had been at home all day on the 12th and found no card anywhere.
pa63.hypothesis: The courier did not attempt delivery on the 12th.

pa64.premise: The Quenby build pipeline runs three stages in order: compile, test, and package. If any stage fails, the later stages are skipped and the pipeline is marked failed. The package stage is also skipped, without failing the pipeline, on any branch other than main. Yesterday's run on the feature branch 'ledger-fix' passed compile and test. The run on main failed at the test stage. There were no other runs.
pa64.hypothesis: Yesterday, neither run produced a package.

pa65.premise: In the Elmbridge chess league, a win is worth 1 point, a draw half a point, and a loss nothing. Hedvig played six games this season: she won three, drew two, and lost one. Her club-mate Anders played the same number of games and finished with exactly one point more than Hedvig. Anders drew no games at all this season.

pa66.premise: Perpetua's passport was issued on 14 February and is valid for ten years from the date of issue. The country she is visiting requires that a visitor's passport remain valid for at least six months after the date of entry. She plans to enter the country on 20 September of the year in which the passport reaches nine and a half years since its issue, and to stay for two weeks.
pa66.hypothesis: Perpetua's passport will satisfy the six-month validity requirement on her planned entry date.

pa67.premise: In the Tamsin Cup final, Redgate scored first, in the ninth minute. Holloway equalised before half time. The only goal of the second half came from a penalty awarded in the seventieth minute, which was converted by Holloway's captain. pa67.hypothesis: The final was decided by a penalty shoot-out.

pa68.premise: The Tollgate car park charges 2 units for the first hour and 3 units for each additional hour or part of an hour, up to a daily maximum of 14 units. Overnight parking is not permitted. Hedda parked at 08:20 and left at 13:05 the same day. She paid the exact amount due at the machine on her way out and kept the receipt for her expenses claim.

pa69.premise: All of the reading group's members have read at least one of the two books chosen for this month. Exactly four members have read both. The group has eleven members, and nobody outside the group attends the meetings or is counted. Seven members have read the first book.
